data.source_title: The impact of teach-back on patient recall and understanding of discharge information in the emergency department: the Emergency Teach-Back (EM-TeBa) study
data.source_setting: Urban non-academic ED; adults discharged with new medical problem
data.quantity: Patients leaving ED with at least one comprehension deficit
data.source_evidence_basis: Original full text XML abstract reports 483 participants (239 control, 244 teach-back) and says the proportion leaving with at least one comprehension deficit declined from 49% to 11.9% after teach-back.
data.limitations: Single-center nonrandomized pre-post comparison, unblinded; language-barrier patients excluded, limiting applicability to interpreter-mediated communication. Does not establish distal outcomes.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Use teach-back to identify/correct comprehension gaps before discharge; excluded language-barrier patients mean this does not establish effectiveness when interpreters are used.
